title: Fourteen of 27 repeated-RI Atlantic storms had at least 20 kt of wind loss before later RI in HURDAT2, 1982-2025
abstract: We tested whether repeated rapid intensification (RI) follows a large wind loss in Atlantic HURDAT2 for 1982-2025. We merged overlapping or touching 24-hour windows with gains of at least 30 kt. This gave 27 multiple-component storms and 29 adjacent component pairs. All main spans had complete tropical six-hour records. Fourteen storms had a chronological wind loss of at least 20 kt after the first RI completion and before a later RI start. Thirteen did not; eight had no sampled wind loss in those spans. The supported fraction was 51.9%, with a conditional 95% three-year block interval of 31.6% to 75.0%. A narrower gap span gave the same storm counts. The result measures the known distinction between repeated fast gains and recovery after wind loss. It does not identify physical storm cycles. One release, rounded winds, land exposure and selected rules limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, an audit and a figure are included. Raw data and record extracts remain external.

display.caption: Wind-loss tests for repeated RI in Atlantic HURDAT2, 1982-2025. Panel A shows storm fractions and conditional 95% three-year block intervals. Panel B shows definition checks at 20 kt loss. Hatched parts are unresolved under a restricted record rule. Labels show supported counts divided by all multiple-component storms. NOAA/NHC supplied the external source.

citations.reason: We use its connected RI window definition and source release. New code tests wind loss. Source overlap means this is not independent data confirmation.
Prior campaign sampling result informed the need to state time rules.
Its methods and discussion allow slow intensification or weakening between RI events. Our test measures that distinction for a different fixed Atlantic sample.
